text:
The Stars have now won five straight, and this one ended with a three-goal burst after Dallas spent most of the night leaning on the Islanders. Jason Robertson scored twice, including the 5-3 goal in the third period, and Mikko Rantanen put the game away at 13:02. Robertson, drafted 39th overall by Dallas in 2017 after a 117-point season for Kingston, finished with two goals and was named the game's first star.

The 6-3 score is a fair reflection of how it went. Dallas took 66 shot attempts to New York's 44 and 38 shots on goal to 20. By expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, the Stars led 3.82 to 1.97. Our deserved-to-win number, the share of simulated replays of every shot that Dallas wins, gives them 79 percent. The third period was the widest gap: 1.44 expected goals for Dallas, 0.32 for New York. The Islanders did hang in, though. Kyle Palmieri's backhand to tie it at 2-2 came on a 5 percent chance, and Brayden Schenn tied it at 3-3 late in the second. Dallas answered with a power-play goal from Justin Hryckowian in between, one of its two chances with the man advantage.

Ilya Sorokin allowed 2.2 more goals than the 38 shots he faced would normally produce. Dallas is on a five-game winning streak. New York leaves without a power-play goal in three tries.
